question: Does the intrinsic direction-bias contrast persist at a withheld larger canonical square size, and how do sector ambiguity and practical loss behave near the directed endpoint?
trigger: Square primary intrinsic contrast resolved at both sizes. Honeycomb arrow intervention changes directed intrinsic risk, while fair relabeling controls pass; mechanism comparisons remain interpretable.
scope: Finite-size mechanism extension at p=.30. L9 is withheld from the first square decision. No thermodynamic extrapolation, transition location or BKT fit.

analysis.unit: independent physical records; paired common activity/sign uniforms across q within this manifest at fixed L,p,n, and all decoders on the same record
analysis.intervals: Pointwise bootstrap95 for exploratory near-directed contrasts; L9 fair-minus-directed uses the existing conservative97.5 interval. Across-size contrasts use independent bootstrap. Gap-CDF fractions get Wilson95 intervals.
analysis.primary: Replicate positive intrinsic fair-minus-directed contrast at withheld L9. Quantify q=.9 and .97 minus q=1 risk and P(|DeltaF|<=1) at each size; inspect full gap CDF, without inferring a universal monotonicity.
analysis.comparison: Stage2/3 samples remain separate. New seed streams are independent of earlier stages. No fit, no stopping based on significance.
analysis.limits: Only three square sizes and one p for extension. Finite q<1 vs q=1 support differences do not establish a thermodynamic singularity.

budget.stopping: fixed sample counts; profile supports L9 with 2,952,423 topology candidates, below12m cap; no approximate substitute
